acceptance: At least three systems complete the admitted Core pilot, covering embedded/in-process, client-server, and distributed or managed-warehouse execution; any substitution requires documented evidence of a materially distinct storage or execution model.
At least one embedded and one client-server reference candidate are evaluated for ranking and sensitivity effects before physical-reference selection.
Alternative block weights and panels are compared with simple baselines and independent holdouts.
Effective weights across all blocks keep every benchmark <=15%, every shared root lineage <=40%, independent real-data work >=25%, and advanced SQL >=15%.
Sensitivity analysis shows the headline does not collapse into one benchmark, capability, lineage, platform, or defensible reference candidate.
The report selects or rejects each workload member and weight with reproducible evidence.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. Numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, thresholds, and the M4 reference remain pilot hypotheses until methodology freeze.
description: Run the candidate methodology on at least three materially different database systems. Use capability coverage, runtime budgets, correlation and sensitivity analysis, and holdout workloads to select membership and weights without tuning the score to DuckDB or one lineage.
